claim: Calibration signal (tracking actual model correctness) and verbalized confidence signal are both linearly decodable from LLM activations but are encoded in orthogonal directions in activation space.
stance_target: verbal confidence fails as a calibration proxy because it is mechanistically disconnected from the model's internal accuracy estimate
scope_conditions: 3 open-weight models, 4 datasets; linear probing and contrastive activation addition (CAA) methodology
quoted_support: calibration and verbalized confidence signals are encoded linearly but are orthogonal to one another -- a finding consistent across three open-weight models and four datasets.

claim: Prompting a model to simultaneously reason (chain-of-thought) and verbalize a confidence score causes the reasoning process to disrupt the verbalized-confidence direction in activation space, worsening miscalibration -- the 'Reasoning Contamination Effect.'
stance_target: using CoT reasoning traces alongside verbal confidence elicitation without controlling for reasoning-induced miscalibration
scope_conditions: same 3-model, 4-dataset setup as the orthogonality finding
quoted_support: when models are prompted to simultaneously reason through a problem and verbalize a confidence score, the reasoning process disrupts the verbalized confidence direction, exacerbating miscalibration. We term this the "Reasoning Contamination Effect."

claim: A two-stage adaptive steering pipeline that reads a model's internal accuracy estimate and steers verbalized output to match it substantially improves calibration alignment across all evaluated models.
stance_target: feasibility of intervention-based fixes for the verbal confidence calibration gap
quoted_support: we introduce a two-stage adaptive steering pipeline that reads the model's internal accuracy estimate and steers verbalized output to match it, substantially improving calibration alignment across all evaluated models.
